Mr. Karan Singh Dugtal, Advocate for the
applicant.
2. Mr. V.S. Pal, A.G.A. for the State.
3. The applicant, who is in judicial custody in
connection with FIR/Case Crime No. 466 of 2026,
under Sections 8 and 20 of NDPS Act, registered
at P.S.-Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar,
has sought his release on bail.
4. As per the prosecution case, the public
caught hold of the applicant near a bus stand,
Rudrapur and thereafter informed to the Police.
Upon receiving such information, Police reached
to the spot, however, prior to their arrival, the two
bags allegedly containing the contraband had
already been opened by the public itself. After
weighing the alleged contraband, which was
suspected to be ganja, the gross weight including
the weight of the bags was found to be 14
kilograms.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that applicant has falsely been implicated
in the case; applicant is 65 years of age and has
come from his native village situated in the State
of Bihar to visit his relative; that the provisions of
Section 50 of the NDPS Act were not complied

with in letter and spirit; that the alleged bag
containing the contraband was already opened by
the public itself prior to the arrival of the Police
team at the spot meaning thereby that the alleged
contraband was not recovered from the conscious
possession of the applicant; that the alleged
contraband is below commercial quantity,
therefore, Section 37 of NDPS Act would not be
attracted in this case; and, that applicant has no
previous criminal history.
6. Learned State Counsel, on the other hand,
has vehemently opposed the bail application.
7. On the last date, State was directed to seek
instructions regarding the criminal history of the
applicant. Today, on instructions, it is submitted
by learned State Counsel that applicant has no
previous criminal history.
8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the records.
9. Having considered the submissions, under
the facts and circumstances of the case and also
considering the fact that the alleged contraband
was not recovered from the conscious possession
of the applicant, the alleged contraband is below
commercial quantity and as such, the applicant
has no previous criminal history, this Court is of
the view that it is a case fit for bail and the
applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
10. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
11. Let the applicant be released on bail on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two
reliable sureties each of the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the court concerned.
 (Alok Mahra J.) 14.10.2026
Ujjwal
